segments.text: Vishnu, keeper of the universe, tore out his own eye. He did it for Shiva, and in return, Shiva gave him the weapon that nothing in the universe can stop, the Sudarshana Chakra. It began with demons. They tormented the gods and killed people. The gods begged Vishnu to save them. Vishnu knew he needed Shiva's power, so he went into the wilderness and worshiped Shiva. Years passed. Shiva did not appear. So Vishnu shaped a lingam, the sacred form of Shiva, out of earth. He chanted the thousand names of Shiva. For every name, he laid one lotus on the lingam. When the chant ended, a thousand lotuses covered it. Shiva was moved, but he wanted to test Vishnu one last time, so he took one lotus away. Vishnu counted the flowers, 999. He searched everywhere, but the lotus was gone. One flower short meant the worship was not complete. Would Vishnu fail in front of Shiva? Then Vishnu smiled. One of his names was Kamalanayana, the one with lotus eyes. His eyes were like lotuses, so one of them could take the place of the flower. He pulled out his own eye and placed it on the lingam, the thousandth lotus. Shiva appeared at once and healed Vishnu's eye. Then he gave him a golden disc with two circles spinning in opposite directions. He named it Sudarshana, which means virtuous vision. That is how Vishnu got the Sudarshana Chakra. Vishnu gave his eye, and Shiva gave him the weapon.
